$comment: Which files make up the corpus. Read by src/corpus.ts.
This exists because assembling the corpus by hand is an input to two
irreversible outputs: a birth's firstSeen is a minimum over whatever files
were concatenated, and an anchor's Merkle root covers exactly the
attestations derived from them. Omit a file and both are wrong in ways that
Every .jsonl in `base` must appear in `include` or `exclude`. A new file
that appears in neither fails the load rather than being silently ignored —
silent omission is the direction that costs a permanent record.

exclude.martian-judged.jsonl: judge output, not reviews — rows carry arm/decisions/fn/fp/judge_fail and no findings
exclude.martian-p3-judged-run1.jsonl: judge output, same shape as martian-judged.jsonl
exclude.martian-repeat-judged.jsonl: judge output, same shape as martian-judged.jsonl
